snippet.title: Commodore 64 Longplay [090] Cisco Heat (EU)
snippet.description:
http://www.longplays.org

Played by: Mad-Matt

Cisco Heat for the Commodore 64 developed by ICE Software and published by Imagesoft  in 1991.

“Cisco heat All American Police Race.  Take the wheel of a high powered police car in this race around the famous areas of San Francisco.  The Golden Gate Bridge. Fisherman’s Wharf, China Town, Twin Peaks all flash by with exciting realism.  Blast the horn to shift other cars out of the way, as you tackle 5 levels of non stop action, but only the best can make it - so hit the gas pedal and race for glory.”

An original Arcade game by Jeleco and converted to Home Computers by ICE.After playing the Spectrum version it would stand to reason to think the game could only get better on other platforms, but then the C64 shows up!  This is 1991 and somehow we got a game that looks like it was a 1986 original racing game that was remade in the arcades years later.  No but really, the C64 version is bad beyond belief.

The Spectrum version for all its faults at least resembled and played like the arcade game but here the games updates at like 2 frames a second and the ai racers just dot around the track and the Position number at the top bares no relation to what is on screen.  Even when on a straight at full speed you can go from 1st to 7th in an instant. The corners come out you so fast you hardly have time to react and it's not as if the game reacts correctly even if you do press the button in time.  The Music is very short and on a constant loop but is passable for resembling the original arcade.

Thankfully, as long as you keep moving and don't run out of time the game seems to be quite easy and completable regardless of your final position.  But overall this conversion is just tragic when compared to greats such as turbo outrun, Power Drift, Chase HQ2 and numerous others.  While the Amiga conversion is much more palatable, it seems more like an Amiga game from 1988 rather than the quality of games from 1991. -
